title: Product PRD: Unified Inference - Overview, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design decisions, roadmap & themes, pricing/packaging notes, and release notes for the Unified Inference product (v8). It is intended for engineering, product, go-to-market, and customer-facing teams to align on scope, timelines, and success criteria.

Background: Redwood's Unified Inference product provides a single developer experience and operational surface for Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. v8 focuses on predictable latency routing, cost-aware model routing, simplified pricing for multi-deployment customers, and observability improvements (per-route cost and quality metrics).

Goals (Top-level)
- Deliver a predictable, unified API and rollout path for customers who want cross-environment consistency.
- Reduce median P50 latency variance by 20% for common generation workloads through smarter routing and autoscaling policies.
- Improve cost visibility and control so customers can reduce per-token unit cost by 10% using recommendations (batching, quantization).
- Provide a pricing and packaging model that increases adoption of Dedicated and Private deployments by making crediting and migration straightforward.

Non-goals
- This release does not include new model architectures or training pipelines.
- This release does not change underlying per-token billing primitives (we will continue per-token measurement).

Product Scope (v8)
1) API & Developer UX - Consistent REST/SDK interface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- New API flag: routing_policy: [latency|cost|region|hybrid] (default: hybrid).
- Streaming improvements: connection keepalive and chunked checkpoints for long responses (>2k tokens).

2) Smart Routing & Fallbacks
- Cost-aware routing engine that evaluates available model variants and infrastructure (GPU profile, region) and selects route based on configured policy.
- Automatic fallback rules: degraded-model fallback, regional fallback, reduced-precision fallback.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds: per-pool error rate > 3% for 5m triggers failover.

3) Observability & Quality Monitoring
- Per-route and per-model dashboards with token-level cost, latency distribution (P50/P90/P99), and quality regressions tied to configured prompt-sets.
- Integrated alert templates: latency > 250ms P90, token-cost delta > 15% over 24h, regression rate > 5% on evaluation prompt-set.

4) Cost Optimization Toolkit (Redwood Optimize integration)
- Suggest batching/window sizes and quantization profiles per workload.
- Apply recommendations in dry-run mode and report estimated savings.

5) Pricing & Packaging Changes
- Introduce a multi-deployment crediting model: Hosted credits can be converted to Dedicated credits at a 0.9x rate during migration windows.
- New Dedicated Starter plan (reserved vCPU/GPU pools) with minimum 3-month commit and predictable per-token baseline.
- Private deployment licensing: add-on for enterprise customers with simplified per-instance licensing and 12-month support bundle.

PRD Requirements (MUST have)
REQ-001: Unified API stability
- The same REST JSON contract for text/chat/embeddings must work without client changes across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Acceptance: SDK test-suite passes 100% in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private nightly gates.
- Owner: eng-developer-experience.

REQ-002: Routing latency SLOs
- For latency routing policy, P95 end-to-end request latency must be <= 300ms for short generation (<=512 tokens) on Dedicated pools sized for workload.
- Measurement: synthetic benchmarks + production telemetry over 7-day window.
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

REQ-003: Cost recommendation engine
- The optimizer must produce at least three actionable recommendations (batching, cache, quantization) per workload with estimated savings and confidence score.
- Acceptance: >= 60% of recommendations yield >=5% cost reduction in A/B tests across sample customers.
- Owner: eng-platform + research.

REQ-004: Billing and crediting model
- Implement conversion API for Hosted->Dedicated credits and UI workflow in Console for migrations, enforcing conversion windows and audit logs.
- Acceptance: End-to-end manual migration tested; billing entries recorded and reconciled in dev billing pipeline.
- Owner: finance-and-legal + eng-platform.

REQ-005: Observability exposures
- Per-route token cost and quality delta must be available in Console and APIs.
- Acceptance: Dashboards render for routes with > 1k daily requests and alerts fire in canary test.
- Owner: eng-platform + eng-sre.

Design & Architecture Notes
- Routing Engine: stateless scoring microservice (routing-score) that queries pool metadata (capacity, region, model-variant), cache hit probability (KV cache), and estimated cost per-token. Ranking implemented as weighted linear score with policy-configurable weights.
- Runtime Integration: Serving runtime exposes a route hint API (route_hint) for quick evaluation; fallback executor supports model-variant switchover with KV cache warmup steps.
- Data Flow: Request -> Auth -> Routing-score -> Inference pool -> Response stream. Telemetry emitted at each hop.
- Security: All migration and credit actions require admin RBAC (role: billing_admin) and audit logs stored for 7 years per compliance guidelines.

Roadmap & Themes (next 6 months)
- Q4 2026 (current release window)
  - Feature-complete implementation of routing engine and API flags.
  - Dedicated Starter plan launch and migration UI beta.
  - Observability dashboards for per-route cost and quality.
- Q1 2027
  - Private licensing GA and 12-month support bundle.
  - Auto-apply recommendation pilot for high-confidence optimizations.
  - Expand region coverage (APAC pilot).
- Metrics to track
  - Adoption: number of customers using routing_policy != default (target: 50 customers in Q4).
  - Performance: P95 latency improvement of 20% baseline on targeted workloads.
  - Economics: average per-token cost reduction of 10% for customers using Optimize recommendations.

Pricing & Packaging Notes
- Pricing principles
  - Transparent unit economics: separate base compute/throughput charge and token usage.
  - Migration-friendly: credits and conversion windows to reduce friction.
  - Predictable tiers: Dedicated Starter, Dedicated Standard, Dedicated Enterprise.

- Example pricing (indicative, final subject to finance review)
  - Hosted: $0.0009 / input-token, $0.0030 / output-token for generation model class G1.
  - Dedicated Starter: $15,000 / month reserved + $0.0018 / output-token over baseline.
  - Private: licensing fee (one-time) + $10,000 / year support bundle.

- Packaging considerations
  - Offer 30-day migration credits conversion window for customers starting Dedicated trials.
  - Enterprise discounts apply for 12+ month commits and volume usage.

Release Notes (v8.0.0)
- Released: 2026-12-05
- Highlights:
  - New routing_policy API flag (hybrid default) and cost-aware routing engine.
  - Dedicated Starter plan and migration UI beta.
  - Console: per-route cost dashboards and quality regression alerts.
  - Integrations: Redwood Optimize recommendations surfaced in Console with dry-run mode.
- Breaking changes:
  - None to existing REST contract; streaming chunk headers adjusted for long-response use (clients may need to re-handle keepalive semantics).
- Known issues:
  - In rare cases (<0.5% of requests), fallback to reduced-precision model variant may increase token-level hallucination rate; research is investigating prompt-specific mitigations.
  - Private installer currently supports only Ubuntu 22.04 for on-prem; RHEL support targeted for Q1 2027.

Rollout Plan
1) Canary (Week 0-2)
- Deploy routing-score to canary clusters (internal + 3 pilot customers).
- Monitor: P95 latency, error rate, cost delta, and quality regressions on prompt-sets.
- Rollback criteria: error rate > 1% sustained for 15m or quality regression > 10% on canary prompt-set.

2) Gradual (Week 3-6)
- Expand to 25% of production traffic with automatic rollback and manual approval gates.
- Run A/B tests for Optimize recommendations on a subset of customers.

3) GA (Week 7)
- Full rollout after safety gate review and finance sign-off on pricing.

Operational Runbooks & Ownership
- Incident triage runbook: eng-sre owns alert response for routing-score incidents. Typical tasks: revert routing policy to region-only, scale Dedicated pools, and open P0.
- Owner matrix:
  - Product (Ava Martinez) - overall product decisions and GTM.
  - Eng-serving-runtime (owner: Jordan Patel) - latency SLOs and runtime integration.
  - Eng-platform (owner: Mei Wong) - Console, billing integration, observability.
  - Finance (owner: Rajesh Rao) - pricing approvals and credit conversions.

Success Metrics (90-day post-GA)
- 50 enterprise customers on Dedicated Starter or higher.
- Average P95 latency improvement of 20% for targeted workloads.
- 10% average cost reduction for customers who applied Optimize recommendations.
